type.label: Questions
type.blurb: The questions He asked, and why
type.intro: Jesus asked far more questions than He answered. Gathered by topic below: what each line of questioning is probing, and where He asks it.

topics.name: Kingdom
topics.description: The reign of God breaking into the world — what it is like, who enters it, and how it grows.

points.title: Which of you by being anxious can add an hour to his life?
points.text: And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to his span of life?
points.summary: Part of a sustained argument that worry is not only painful but useless.

points.title: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
points.text: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
points.summary: Told His family is outside asking for Him, He redraws the family line around obedience.

points.title: Who do you say that I am?
points.text: But who do you say that I am?
points.summary: The hinge of the gospels. He asks what the crowds think first, then makes it personal.

points.title: What is written in the Law? How do you read it?
points.text: What is written in the Law? How do you read it?
points.summary: A lawyer tests Him with a question. He answers with two questions and lets the man convict himself.

points.title: Whose likeness and inscription is this?
points.text: Whose likeness and inscription is this?
points.summary: Handed a trap about taxes, He asks for a coin and turns the question back on them.

topics.name: Faith
topics.description: Trust that acts. Where Jesus found it, where He marvelled at its absence, and what He said it could do.

topics.name: Salvation
topics.description: Being found, forgiven, and given life — why He came and what He came to accomplish.

points.title: Why do you call me good?
points.text: Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
points.summary: A rich man opens with flattery. Jesus refuses it and goes straight to the man's real problem.
